definitions.explanation: The date until which a food product is expected to retain its best quality and taste when stored properly. Products may still be safe to eat after this date.

examples.japanese: {賞味期限|しょうみきげん}を{確認|かくにん}してから{買|か}う。
examples.english: I check the best-before date before buying.

examples.japanese: {賞味期限|しょうみきげん}が{切|き}れている。
{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}は{来月|らいげつ}までです。
examples.english: The best-before date is until next month.

examples.japanese: {賞味期限|しょうみきげん}が{近|ちか}い{商品|しょうひん}は{安|やす}くなっている。
examples.english: Products near their best-before date are discounted.

examples.japanese: {賞味期限|しょうみきげん}を{過|す}ぎても、すぐに{食|た}べられなくなるわけではない。
examples.english: Just because the best-before date has passed doesn't mean the food is immediately inedible.

notes:
COMPOUND: {賞味|しょうみ} (appreciation of taste) + {期限|きげん} (time limit)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}が{切|き}れる (best-before date expires)
・{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}{内|ない}に{食|た}べる (eat within the best-before date)
・{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}が{近|ちか}い (best-before date is approaching)

DISTINCTION: {賞味期限|しょうみきげん} (best-before) refers to quality, while {消費期限|しょうひきげん} (use-by) refers to safety. Products past their {賞味期限|しょうみきげん} may still be safe but may have reduced quality.
